console-over-usb.note: USB Mini-Type B Port (chapter 1): the switch has "a USB mini-Type B console connection on the front panel, and the RJ-45 console port on the switch's rear panel", console input is active on one at a time and the USB connector takes precedence. The mini-B receptacle is `std/mini-usb@1`, placed in the band above the first block between the CONSOLE lamp and the USB Type A port, centred about 66.5 mm in and level with the USB Type A port (Figures 1-1 and 1-8, an estimate like the rest of the front).

ears-and-rack.note: Rack-Mounting a Switch and Attaching the Rack-Mount Brackets (chapter 2): "The 19-inch brackets are included with the switch", attached with four screws "for the front-mounting or rear-mounting positions (Figure 2-8)", and "Use four screws to attach the brackets for the front-mounting position". Figure 2-8 shows the bracket on the front and on the rear end of the side wall, so the front-mounting position is the one shipped and the rear-mounting position the other. NO FIGURE DIMENSIONS EITHER POSITION, so no `at` is written. Figure 2-7 lists RACK-KIT-T1= (19, 23, 24 inch and ETSI brackets) and 4PT-KIT-T1= (extension rails for four-point mounting); neither is a library part yet (see the gaps).

gate-1.note: THE FIGURES ARE PERSPECTIVE DRAWINGS, NOT ELEVATIONS, so every position is an estimate. Figure 1-1 is 1280 x 440 px with the face seen from the right and above: its height reads 84 px at the left end and about 109 px at the right, so the scale grows by about a third along the face and no single px/mm holds. The anchors are the 17.5 in width (face edge to face edge, 24 to 982 px, 2.15 px/mm on average) and the RJ-45 pitch, 13.97 mm, which reads 2.08 px/mm in the first block and 2.36 px/mm in the fourth. Figure 1-8, the left end close up, is nearer square-on and gives the vertical order: the face 12.8 px/mm tall, the jack openings at 8.4 and 20.4 mm down, the lamp strip at 34.5 mm, and the mode button, lamp pills, mini-B and USB-A in a band above the jacks. Good to about 3 mm along the face near the left and 8 mm near the right, 1 mm across it.

interface-names.note: NOT IN THE GUIDE. Port naming lives in the IOS configuration guides, which are not held, so no `interfaces:` block is written. The NetBox community type for this model names GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/48 and TenGigabitEthernet1/1/1 to 1/1/4 (netbox-community/devicetype-library, device-types/Cisco/ WS-C3650-48PD-L.yaml); that is a community file and is not carried.

lamps.note: Front Panel (chapter 1), Figure 1-8: STAT, DUPLX, SPEED, STACK and PoE are the mode lamps beside the mode button, SYST and ACTV beneath them, and the CONSOLE lamp beside the USB mini-B port. Table 1-2 (SYST): off, green normal, blinking green POST, blinking amber a power supply or fan fault, amber receiving power but not functioning. Table 1-3 and Table 1-4 (port LEDs by mode): in STAT mode off is no link, green link, blinking green activity, alternating green-amber a link fault, amber blocked by spanning tree; the other modes read speed, duplex, active switch and PoE state. Table 1-5 (USB console): off disabled, green enabled. Table 1-6 (ACTV): off not the active switch, green active or standalone, amber an election or stack error, slow blinking green standby. Table 1-9 (uplink): off, green link, blinking green activity, blinking amber a fault or limit, amber disabled. The guide's blink patterns are not states a drawing can hold, so each lamp lists its steady colours.

port-order.note: Figures 1-1 and 1-8: each block of twelve prints one up-arrow and one down-arrow lamp under each column, with "01X" at the left end of the strip and "12X" at the right, "13X" and "24X" under the second, "25X" and "36X" under the third and "37X" and "48X" under the fourth. So the odd port is the upper jack and numbering runs down each column. Only the ends of each strip are printed, so only they are drawn.

power.note: Table 1-1: 640 W power supply. Table 1-13: 48-port PoE switch, default supply PWR-C2-640WAC, 390 W of PoE available; Table 1-14: 390 W with one 640 W DC supply and 780 W with two; Table 1-15: PoE+ on 48 ports needs two 1025 W supplies, and PoE (15.4 W) needs one 1025 W or two 640 W. Table 1-1 prints no typical or maximum draw for the switch itself and none is stated here.

rear-face.note: Figure 1-13, read as fractions of the rear face (62 to 1000 px for 444.5 mm, 2.11 px/mm): at the left the ground connector (callout 1, two threaded holes with the ground symbol between), the RJ-45 console port (2) over the RJ-45 management port (3) with their legend CONSOLE and MGMT beneath; three fan modules (4) with a StackWise port (5) in the gap after the first and after the second; two supply bays (8) at the right, each with the AC OK (6) and PS OK (7) lamps. The supplies read 95 mm wide, which agrees with spec Table 1-2's 3.75 in. The fan modules read 44 mm wide, which fixes the face of spec Table 1-5 (see cisco/fan-t1).

rear-lamps.note: Table 1-12 (RJ-45 console): off is disabled with USB console active, green enabled with USB console disabled. Table 1-23 (Ethernet management port): green link up without activity, blinking green link and activity, off link down. The supplies' AC OK and PS OK lamps are Table 1-21 and the fan LED is green when the fan runs and amber when it fails (Fan Modules, chapter 1).

rows.note: Figure 1-8: the upper jacks stand with the latch at the top and the lower with it at the bottom, the usual stacked mirror, so the top row is turned 180 as the registry's rj45-ganged is drawn. The openings read 9.7 mm tall and 2 mm apart, so a 12.0 mm row pitch of 11.0 mm jacks.

sources.note: One source, not committed: Cisco Catalyst 3650 Switches Hardware Installation Guide, September 2016, OL-29734-01, 126 pages (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst3650/hardware/installation/guide/Cat3650hig_book.pdf). Table 1-1 (PDF p15-20) is the switch models table; the Technical Specifications appendix (from PDF p103) restarts its table numbers, so "spec Table 1-1", "spec Table 1-2" and "spec Table 1-5" below are the appendix's. Its figures are isometric line drawings that it says are "not intended to depict any particular color scheme" (Front Panel, PDF p21). No data sheet, no flat elevation, no photograph and no 3D model of any 3650 is held. The front is Figure 1-1 (the 48PD-L) with the left end enlarged in Figure 1-8; the rear is Figure 1-13. THE NETBOX COMMUNITY DEVICE TYPES for this model were read as a second opinion on the port list only and carry nothing else here.

stackwise.note: StackWise Ports (chapter 1): "StackWise adapter blanks installed in the StackWise ports is the default setup", and a stack needs adapters installed; "You cannot have a switch stack containing a mix of Catalyst 3650 and Catalyst 3850 switches". The adapters and cables are sold as C3650-STACK-KIT=, and no figure draws the adapter's own face, so the bays accept only the blank here.

the-envelope.note: spec Table 1-1: "Catalyst 3650 48-port PoE+ switches 1.73 x 17.5 x 17.625 in. (4.4 x 44.5 x 44.8 cm)", H x W x D, for the chassis assembly as it is shipped: three fans, two StackWise adapter blanks, one power supply blank and the default power supply. 17.5 in is 444.5 mm and 17.625 in 447.7 mm. 1.73 IN IS THE GUIDE'S NOMINAL 1RU: the same box is printed 1.75 in (4.45 cm) in other guides, neither is measured, and 44.45 mm is carried. One row of the table covers every 24- and 48-port PoE+ model, and the 48-port PoE+ row was read for this model. Weight 16.75 lb (7.6 kg) from the same table's 48-port PoE row. The 1025 W supply is 1.5 in deeper than the others (spec Table 1-2), and the table's own deeper row, 19.125 in, belongs to the 48-port Full PoE models; no deeper figure is printed for a PoE+ model carrying that supply.

the-four-blocks.note: Figure 1-1: four windows of twelve jacks, six columns by two rows, 174 px wide in the first and 198 px in the fourth, which is 83.8 mm of 13.97 mm pitch each. The first jack opening starts about 9 mm in from the face edge (Figure 1-8 and Figure 1-1 agree to 0.5 mm once the edge is read at 24 px, not at the window frame), and the windows are separated by a bar about 2 mm wide, so the block step is 85.8 mm. The fourth block is then read 266.7 mm in against 268 to 270 mm from the figure's right-hand scale.

uplinks.note: Figure 1-1 draws the uplink module at the right: two long vent slots, the legend "Catalyst 3650 48PoE+ 2X10G", four cages and under them G1, G2, G3 TE3 and G4 TE4 with a lamp beside each. Uplink Ports (chapter 1): "Two slots (left side) supporting only 1-Gigabit SFP modules and two slots (right side) supporting either 10-Gigabit SFP+ modules or 1-Gigabit SFP modules", and Table 1-1 gives this model two 1G SFP and two 10G SFP+ uplinks. "An SFP+ module ports has two labels, G(x) and TE(x)". The cages read about 16.4 mm apart, wider than the registry's 14.25 mm abutting pitch, so they are placed on that pitch. The vent slots and the legend are read as fractions of the module's height.
